subject: Mobile Development
title: How the Touch Screen Talks to the OS
description: A short lesson to help you apply How the Touch Screen Talks to the OS.

hook.text: You press a button on screen. Electricity, circuits, and software all react in milliseconds.

buildup.text: A capacitive grid detects where your finger touches by measuring electrical field changes.

discovery.text: A touch controller chip converts the raw signal into coordinates 120 times per second.

twist.text: The OS must predict where your finger is going to reduce perceived latency.

climax.text: Touch feels instant because hardware and software conspire to hide every delay.

quiz.question: How do phones reduce perceived touch latency?
options: By predicting where your finger is going
